newsitem.title: USA: U.S. driver fails in world land speed record bid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. driver fails in world land speed record bid.

text.p: An American driver's attempt to set a new world land speed record failed on Monday when his jet-powered car tilted onto its side and spun around at 675 miles per hour (1,086 kph), a spokesman said.

Craig Breedlove, 59, attempting to set a new world mark in Nevada's Black Rock Desert 31 years after pushing the record to 600.601 mph (966.5 kph), was not hurt, but his car "Spirit of America II" was damaged, spokesman Marc Samson said.
Samson blamed a gusty cross-wind, although he said Breedlove was going faster than planned.
"He had too much juice, he wasn't planning on going that fast," Samson said.
Breedlove, who set five world land speed records between 1963 and 1965, was trying to beat the record of 633.47 mph (1,019 kph) set 13 years ago by Richard Noble of Britain.
The American has been forced to call off his record bid for this year because of Nevada's coming rainy season, but he aims to try again next spring, Samson said.
"There's not a huge amount of damage, but enough that he's done for the season," he said. "He's in good spirits. He wasn't scratched."
To set a new mark, Breedlove had to drive at record speed over one mile (1.6 km) twice in opposite directions at the desert site, about 100 miles (160 km) north of Reno.
Breedlove entered the timed mile at 675 mph (1,086 kph) in his dart-shaped car, well above the record speed, Samson said.
The car tilted and did a U-turn, but Breedlove managed to slow it down and it ended upright, Samson said. The side of the car scraped the desert, damaging the left wheel well.
He said the team was not sure of all the reasons why the car was destabilised and would have to study computer data.

Breedlove has spent five years and $5 million on his bid to recapture the record. His car is powered by a J-79 General Electric jet engine from a Navy F-4 Phantom fighter that produces the equivalent of 45,000 horsepower.
His is one of several teams around the world whose ultimate dream is to raise the land speed record to 760 mph (1,223 kph) and break the speed of sound.
Britain's Thrust SSC jet car, designed by Noble and driven by Andy Green, is undergoing trials in a Jordon desert in preparation for a bid to break the sound barrier next year.
